h1. *Description:*

This task involves developing the front-end and basic back-end functionality for the Shift Giving web and mobile applications, leveraging AI code generation tools to accelerate development. We will use [AI Tool Name - e.g., GitHub Copilot, Tabnine, Amazon CodeWhisperer] to generate code based on our existing wireframes and backlog. The focus will be on creating a functional and user-friendly interface that aligns with the Shift Giving project goals.

h1. *User Acceptance Testing (UAT):*

* *Functionality:*
** Users can successfully navigate through all screens and sections of the app.
** Users can input data into forms and the data is correctly saved and/or processed (e.g., user registration, donation forms).
** Users can interact with all interactive elements (buttons, links, etc.) as expected.
** The app functions correctly across different browsers and devices (responsive design).
* *Usability:*
** The app's interface is intuitive and easy to understand.
** The app's design is consistent with the provided wireframes and branding guidelines.
** The app provides clear instructions and feedback to the user.
* *Performance:*
** The app loads quickly and performs smoothly.
** There are no noticeable bugs or errors.

*Engineering Details:*

# *Environment Setup:*
#* Set up development environment with necessary tools and frameworks (e.g., React, Node.js, relevant mobile development framework).
#* Integrate the chosen AI code generation tool into the IDE.
# *Front-End Development:*
#* Use the provided wireframes and backlog to define the app's structure and functionality.
#* Leverage the AI code generation tool to generate code for UI components, layouts, and basic interactions.
#* Refine and customize the generated code to meet specific design requirements and ensure code quality.
#* Implement responsive design to ensure compatibility across different devices.
# *Back-End Development (Basic):*
#* Set up basic back-end functionality for handling user input and data persistence (e.g., using Firebase, a simple Node.js server).
#* Utilize AI code generation to assist with basic API endpoint creation and data handling logic.
#* Ensure secure handling of user data.
# *Testing:*
#* Conduct thorough unit and integration testing to identify and fix any bugs or errors.
#* Perform cross-browser and cross-device testing to ensure compatibility.
# *Code Review:*
#* Submit code for review by a senior engineer to ensure code quality and adherence to best practices.

*Additional Notes:*

* This is actually from Eric
** Feel free to leverage whatever AI tool. We’ll start with ChatGPT but if that doesn’t work we can figure out CoPilot, Amazon CodeWhiperer, etc. 
** Team level ChatGPT account in 1 pass 
* The AI code generation tool should be used as an aid to accelerate development, not as a replacement for critical thinking and problem-solving.
* Generated code must be thoroughly reviewed and tested to ensure quality and security.
* This card focuses on the initial development of the web and mobile apps. Future cards will address more advanced features and functionalities.

column125:
22/May/24 1:25 PM;60d9d4117d016900700bbaab;h3. 1. Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM)

* Supports both Android and iOS.
* Easy integration with React Native.
* Provides analytics and insights.
* Supports various types of messages
* Can create custom audiences for targeted notifications using analytics
** Less robust than OneSignal
** More complex setup than OneSignal
* Ability to deliver Web Push Notifications
* Free
* Experience at Shift working with it

*References:*

* [Firebase Cloud Messaging|https://firebase.google.com/docs/cloud-messaging]
* [React Native Firebase FCM|https://rnfirebase.io/]
* [Firebase Analytics Audiences|https://firebase.google.com/docs/analytics]

h3. 2. OneSignal

* Supports both iOS and Android.
* Specialized service for messaging.
** Noted for it’s ease of use
** Mobile push, web push, in-app messaging, email, and SMS
* React Native SDK out of the box
* Ability for advanced segmentation and targeting.
** Demographics/behaviors/preferences/device/platform
* Rich media notifications and analytics.
* Ability to deliver Web Push Notifications
* User-friendly dashboard for managing notifications
* Free tier limitations.
** Unlimited push notifications to a maximum of 10,000 subscribers at once
** 6 audience segments, 2 data tags
* Learning curve
* Dependency on a third-party service.

*References:*

* [OneSignal Documentation|https://documentation.onesignal.com/docs/react-native-sdk-setup]
* [OneSignal Segments|https://documentation.onesignal.com/docs/segmentation]
* [OneSignal vs. FCM|https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/onesignal-vs-firebase-fcm-mostafa-morsy-x5bxc/]

h3. 4. Expo Push Notifications (if using Expo)

* Supports both iOS and Android.
* Simplifies setup and management.
* Requires Expo's managed workflow.
* Less control compared to FCM or OneSignal.
* Limited segmentation and targeting (would require integration with another service, like Firebase)

*References:*

* [Expo Push Notifications|https://docs.expo.dev/push-notifications/overview/]

h3. 4. React Native Push Notifications Library

* Supports both iOS and Android.
* Simplifies the integration of FCM and APNS.
* Offers local and scheduled notifications.
* Currently used in GHC
* Outdated repo (last release was 2021)
* Does not offer segmentation/targeting (custom logic in backend required to implement)

*References:*

* [React Native Push Notifications|https://github.com/zo0r/react-native-push-notification]
